clue.text: Second drink in isolated spot

parts.note: to second a motion is to back it

explanation.surface: Someone orders another round in a remote country pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second' looks like a number or a time unit, but it is the verb meaning support.
explanation.definitionFit: A backwater is a quiet place cut off from the main currents of activity, so a remote and sleepy spot.

clue.text: A nervous wreck in box, on trial

indicators.note: in a down entry one piece sitting on another comes above it, so the first part is written first

parts.note: a basket is a woven box or container
a case heard in court is a trial

explanation.surface: A defendant shaking in the dock while on trial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In box' suggests the witness box or dock, but box is just the container that starts the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Basket case is an informal idiom for a person too anxious or stressed to cope.

clue.text: Group of singers sing endlessly about love

indicators.note: about means going around, so the shortened verb wraps the other piece
without an end means the final letter of that word is dropped

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: Choristers belting out love songs without stopping.
explanation.walkthrough: CHIRP loses its last letter to become CHIR, which is split around O.
explanation.definitionFit: A choir is an organised body of singers, as in a church or concert ensemble.

clue.text: Perform a baptism to celebrate a birth

definitions.meaning: first meaning: literally pour water over an infant's head at the font
second meaning: the British idiom for having a celebratory drink after a child is born

explanation.surface: A christening held in honour of a newborn.
explanation.walkthrough: In British usage the phrase means going for a drink to toast a new baby; the literal sense is the christening splash.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is both the literal act at a christening and a British idiom for drinking a toast to a newborn.

clue.text: Can one holding drill start to repair a kitchen utensil?

indicators.note: one thing holding another keeps it inside, so a piece goes within the word for one

parts.note: physical exercise, as in a gym drill

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter, so only that letter is taken

explanation.surface: Asks whether someone holding a drill can fix a kitchen gadget.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Can' reads as a verb asking about ability; it is the noun tin. PE stands for physical education, school exercise drills.
explanation.definitionFit: A tin opener is the household tool used for cutting the lid off a can of food.

clue.text: Royal feast cut short

indicators.note: something cut short loses its end, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: to regale is to feast or entertain lavishly

explanation.surface: A royal banquet that ends early.
explanation.definitionFit: Regal is a synonym describing something fit for or belonging to a king or queen.

clue.text: Glimpse object of especial interest

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to catch a view of something
second meaning: a notable attraction, as in seeing the city's attractions

explanation.surface: Catching a brief view of something remarkable.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb the word means spot or catch sight of; as a noun it is a tourist attraction worth seeing.

clue.text: I'm unfortunately turned over by trick, a computer fraud

indicators.note: something turned over is flipped end to end, so the opening words are read backwards

parts.note: taken as written, minus the apostrophe
alas is said when something is unfortunate
a trick is a method or knack for doing something

explanation.surface: Someone confesses they have been sadly upended by a con.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unfortunately' looks like an anagram signal but means ALAS; IM followed by ALAS, read backwards, makes the sausage word.
explanation.definitionFit: A salami technique is a cyber-crime that skims tiny sums from many transactions, slice by slice.

clue.text: New measuring device, reportedly for fruit

indicators.note: what is reported is heard rather than read, so the word is taken by its pronunciation

parts.note: a gauge measures, and is pronounced like this spelling

explanation.surface: A newly invented measuring device said to be for fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: A greengage is a kind of sweet green plum, so it is a variety of fruit.

clue.text: Film and play opening in Soho

parts.note: to toy with something is to play with it

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter, so only that letter is kept

explanation.surface: A film and a play premiering in London's Soho entertainment district.
explanation.walkthrough: Soho is the London district of theatres and film companies, which makes the surface plausible.
explanation.definitionFit: Toys is the 1992 comedy film starring Robin Williams, a specific title rather than a synonym.

clue.text: Taking photographs of spectators where marksmen practise

parts.note: the crowd watching, as at a golf tournament, is the gallery

explanation.surface: A photographer snapping the crowd at a shooting range.
explanation.definitionFit: A shooting gallery is an indoor range or fairground booth where people fire at targets.

clue.text: Land shortage ignored by duke

indicators.note: what is ignored is left out, so that letter is removed

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for duke

explanation.surface: A duke who disregards a shortage of land on his estate.
explanation.definitionFit: Earth means the ground or soil, so it serves as a synonym for land.

clue.text: Maintenance allowance Olympian squandered

indicators.note: money squandered is scattered carelessly, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: An athlete who wasted the support payments they received.
explanation.definitionFit: Palimony is support paid to a former unmarried partner after a split, a form of maintenance.

clue.text: Amity shown by female diner relaxed on liner

indicators.note: in a down entry one part on another sits above it, so the earlier pieces come first

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for female

indicators.note: something relaxed has loosened up, so these letters are loosened into a new order

parts.note: an ocean liner is a ship

explanation.surface: Passengers become friendly as a woman relaxes at dinner on a cruise.
explanation.definitionFit: Amity is peaceful goodwill between people, which is the close bond of being friends.

clue.text: Literary character, jumping bail, put in prison

indicators.note: something put in another goes inside it
letters that are jumping move about and land in a new order

explanation.surface: A fictional figure who skipped bail and ended up behind bars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jumping bail' is the idiom for absconding, but here it shuffles the four letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Caliban is the monstrous servant of Prospero in Shakespeare's play The Tempest.

clue.text: Rule at sea confused eminent poets

indicators.note: something confused is muddled up, so these letters are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: Great poets baffled by maritime law.
explanation.definitionFit: Poets laureate are honoured poets, often appointed to an official post, so the word names distinguished poets.

clue.text: Likely to remain fine in South, possibly after about one

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for south

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the rearranged word goes around the number
possibly signals one of several arrangements, so the word beside it is rearranged

explanation.surface: A weather forecast: fine conditions expected in the south after around one o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' looks like a time word, but it is the letters to be rearranged around I.
explanation.definitionFit: Set fair is a weather phrase, shown on barometers, meaning settled conditions expected to continue.

clue.text: Dope easy to name

parts.note: N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: Saying a stupid person is easy to identify.
explanation.definitionFit: A dope is a slang word for a fool or idiot, the same as a gullible, dim person.

clue.text: After last of nightmares, refuse to sleep

indicators.note: one piece after another means it is written following it
the last of a word is its final letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: lumber is junk or discarded rubbish

explanation.surface: Someone who, after bad dreams, will not go back to sleep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' reads as the verb decline; it is the noun meaning rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Slumber is a literary synonym for sleep, either as a noun or a verb.

clue.text: Pal carrying revolutionary weapon

indicators.note: something carrying another holds it within, so one piece goes inside the other

explanation.surface: A friend armed with a rebel's gun.
explanation.definitionFit: A machete is a broad heavy blade used for cutting vegetation and as a weapon.

clue.text: Cop loses out in a disgusting place

indicators.note: out means wrong or disordered, so the letters before it are put in a different order

explanation.surface: A police officer who loses a suspect in a filthy area.
explanation.definitionFit: A cesspool is a pit for sewage, and by extension any vile or corrupt place.

clue.text: Proprietor in state of depression having day off

indicators.note: having a day off means taking leave, so the abbreviation for day leaves the word

parts.note: a downer is a gloomy state or spell

explanation.surface: A shop proprietor feeling low and taking a day off.
explanation.definitionFit: Proprietor is a formal synonym for the person who holds a business or property.

clue.text: Itinerant US actor making a comeback

indicators.note: a comeback goes back the way it came, so the name is read in the opposite direction

explanation.surface: A wandering American actor who returns to the screen.
explanation.definitionFit: A nomad is a person with no fixed home, so the word can stand for itinerant.

clue.text: Upset mason grumbles

indicators.note: something upset is knocked over and disarranged, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An unhappy builder complaining.
explanation.definitionFit: To moan is to complain, so moans is a synonym of grumbles as a verb.

clue.text: Efficient porter grabbing first of bags

indicators.note: something grabbing holds a thing in its grip, so a letter goes inside
the first of a word is its opening letter alone

explanation.surface: A capable hotel porter seizing the luggage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Porter' looks like a luggage carrier, but it is a kind of beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Able means competent or capable, close in sense to efficient.

clue.text: Fruit British head dropped into perfect drink

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for British
nut is slang for the head
squash is a British fruit cordial diluted with water

explanation.surface: A British person's head dunked into a perfect drink.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces simply run on in order: B, UTTER, NUT, SQUASH. Squash is a sweet fruit concentrate Britons dilute to drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Botanically a squash is a fruit, as it carries seeds, though cooks treat it as a vegetable.

clue.text: Helped let learner driver out

indicators.note: out means left out, so that letter is removed from the word

parts.note: to let a property is to lease it
L plates mark a learner driver in Britain

explanation.surface: An instructor helped a learner driver out of the car.
explanation.definitionFit: Eased means made something easier or less difficult, so it can mean helped or assisted.

clue.text: As good as gold? Not us

definitions.meaning: surface reading: the phrase for a well-behaved child
setter's reading: competitors speaking who finished just short of the gold medal

explanation.surface: Children admitting they have not been well behaved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As good as gold' is a saying about obedience, but read literally it asks who equalled the winner.
explanation.definitionFit: Those placed second take silver, not gold, so they are by definition not as good as the winner.
